external_sources.title: MoneyHelper Budget planner
external_sources.supports: A budget compares money in and spending over the same period. Classroom amounts are fictional; pupils do not open accounts or disclose finances.

external_sources.title: GOV.UK Accepting returns and giving refunds: the law
external_sources.supports: Faulty goods and an in-shop change of mind are different. A change of mind alone does not create a legal refund right for ordinary goods bought in person. Proof of purchase can take more than one form. Specific remedies depend on the facts; no automatic refund promise is made.

external_sources.title: National Careers Service Explore careers
external_sources.supports: Job profiles help check tasks, skills, entry requirements and possible routes. Classroom role cards are simplified authored examples, not quotations or guarantees of entry.

external_sources.title: HSE Introduction to managing health and safety
external_sources.supports: Employers must provide suitable information, training and supervision for safe work. A new worker should ask for instruction rather than attempt unfamiliar equipment.

external_sources.title: PSHE Association Handling complex issues safely
external_sources.supports: Use ground rules, fictional scenarios, the right to pass and the setting safeguarding response.

evidence.description: Individual job-task and skill link, a route question, and an adult-responsibility scenario response with support and response after feedback.

routes.Aspire: Aspire: compare the jobs and a route to check.

cases.text: A cafe worker is unsure of an order. They ask the customer to repeat it.
cases.fact: They check what the customer wants.
cases.next_step: Listen, repeat the order and check it is right.
cases.staff_note: Links listening and clear speech to the task. A quiet supported response is valid.

cases.text: A stock worker checks each label against the list before putting items away.
cases.next_step: Follow the agreed storage task and ask about a mismatch.
cases.staff_note: Links reading/checking detail to the role; do not imply that speed matters more than accuracy.

cases.text: Taylor’s bus is late for work. Taylor decides not to tell anyone.
cases.fact: The workplace will not know about the delay.
cases.next_step: Contact the named supervisor using the agreed route.
cases.staff_note: A late bus can be outside the person’s control. Assess the communication choice without blame.

cases.text: A new worker is asked to use a machine. They have not had training.
cases.fact: The worker has not been shown safe use.
cases.next_step: Pause and ask the supervisor for training and support.
cases.staff_note: No live machinery or unsafe role-play. Employer duties remain; responsibility is not only on the worker.

cases.text: Robin has a bill due soon. Robin puts the date in a planner and checks the amount.
cases.fact: Robin keeps track of the date and cost.
cases.next_step: Plan for the bill and ask for help if the money is short.
cases.staff_note: An adult-life example, not an instruction for pupils to pay a bill or disclose family debt.

cases.text: Kai likes a job title but does not know its tasks, skills or entry route.
cases.fact: The title alone is not enough to choose a route.
cases.next_step: Use a job profile with a careers adviser to check the role.
cases.staff_note: Different jobs and learners may use different routes. Do not guarantee a vacancy or qualification outcome.

We Do: 5 minutes.

The scheme’s December assessment stays in December. Today supplies formative work towards the named adult-life unit; it does not complete an award. Public award labels are masked only.
Purpose and success checks
What helps someone get ready for work?
I can link a job task to a useful skill. I can name a route or question to explore. I can choose a responsible next step.
LAUNCH-PSHE-W2-E1: Individual job-task and skill link, a route question, and an adult-responsibility scenario response with support and response after feedback.
Before pupils arrive

Prepare the deck, Evidence Sheet and Vocabulary Mat for each learner; one set of Support Cards; pens, timer and spare paper. Use the two printed role cards on Support Cards page 3. Read the Staff Answers. No log-ins, live transactions, employer contact or web search is needed.

Identify the staff member and agreed place for private help. Read the local safeguarding route. Offer a quiet seat, processing time and a supported break. Pupils may work alongside each other or with an adult; capture each person’s own evidence.
Calendar
W2 runs Monday 9 to Friday 13 November. No fixed lesson day or clock slot was supplied. Enter the actual teaching date above; do not assume a Monday lesson in W1.

Min
Action

Describe the fictional picture; hear a clue or question.
Read the scheme objective and three I can checks.

Finish the individual two-page Evidence Sheet.

Keep the vocabulary mat available throughout.
Hidden reference for adults.
Hinge and reteach

C. Ask the supervisor to explain and show the safe task before attempting it. Employers must provide suitable training and supervision. A and B do not establish safe competence. Asking for support is responsible; being an adult does not mean doing everything alone. If the reason is missing, re-model the key distinction and try a fresh case. A correct letter alone is not evidence of understanding.
Access routes

Supported: choose from the two role cards; read C and D aloud and scribe the learner’s reason. Independent: link a task and skill, consider all six cases and explain a next step. Aspire: compare both roles and name a route or missing fact to check.

Begin evidence during the 12-minute practice; use the six-minute capture to finish it. Accept pointing, speech, drawing or writing. Read and scribe without supplying the assessed reason. No forced pair work, cold calling or public performance.
Safe discussion evidence and learner voice
Boundaries and private help

Use fictional adults, roles and bills. Do not ask pupils to describe family employment, benefit claims or caring duties. Do not operate machinery or contact real employers. A class role card is a starting point for discussion, not a promise of entry, pay or vacancy.

Keep cases fictional and allow a pass or a private alternative. If a concern arises, listen calmly, do not investigate in class or promise secrecy, and follow local safeguarding procedures. Keep safeguarding records separate from learning evidence. Help the learner reach another trusted adult if needed.
Assessment and feedback

Cafe assistant: listening helps check an order; clear speech helps confirm it. Stock assistant: checking details helps match items to a list. Accept other justified links. Route questions may ask about training, entry requirements, supported routes or work experience. For C, communicate the delay; D, pause and seek training; E, plan the payment and seek help if short.

Retain the actual working, reason, response mode and support. A copied model or blank form is not completed evidence. Use VF · WS · I · NS+ (Yellow Box) · // (self-edit) · ? (read back) · R (responded) · E (evidence in the school's evidence record). R requires Voice, Audience, an NS+ prompt and the learner’s response in their own colour. Record E only when evidence has actually been banked.
Lundy moments

Space: a calm, non-personal way to respond. Voice: choose a view and explain it. Audience: the teaching adult listens or reads, then replies. Influence: record the learner’s requested support or next task and what changes as a result.
Speaking listening and writing

Possible communication evidence: explain a task-and-skill link, listen to a work instruction, ask for clarification and write or dictate a message about a delay. The receiving teacher maps authentic responses to their own portfolio requirements. No communication criteria are assigned here.

Teacher model and hinge

Alex starts a stockroom role. Task: check boxes against a list. Skill: check details with care. Alex asks for the task to be shown. Alex checks the start time and travel plan. If unsure, Alex asks the supervisor.

C. Ask the supervisor to explain and show the safe task before attempting it. Employers must provide suitable training and supervision. A and B do not establish safe competence. Asking for support is responsible; being an adult does not mean doing everything alone.
Individual evidence key

Cafe assistant: listening helps check an order; clear speech helps confirm it. Stock assistant: checking details helps match items to a list. Accept other justified links. Route questions may ask about training, entry requirements, supported routes or work experience. For C, communicate the delay; D, pause and seek training; E, plan the payment and seek help if short.
Feedback and safe teaching
Case A: Links listening and clear speech to the task. A quiet supported response is valid.
Case B: Links reading/checking detail to the role; do not imply that speed matters more than accuracy.
Case C: A late bus can be outside the person’s control. Assess the communication choice without blame.
Case D: No live machinery or unsafe role-play. Employer duties remain; responsibility is not only on the worker.
Case E: An adult-life example, not an instruction for pupils to pay a bill or disclose family debt.
Case F: Different jobs and learners may use different routes. Do not guarantee a vacancy or qualification outcome.
Common misunderstandings

A job title does not tell us every task or entry requirement. Skills can develop with practice and support. Adult responsibility includes asking for help. Unpaid caring and volunteering also use skills; paid employment is not a measure of a person’s worth.
Teaching boundary

Use fictional adults, roles and bills. Do not ask pupils to describe family employment, benefit claims or caring duties. Do not operate machinery or contact real employers. A class role card is a starting point for discussion, not a promise of entry, pay or vacancy.
Response and next teaching step

If the reason is vague, return to the case words or working. If a fact is missing, ask what must be checked and with whom. Re-model one new example, then retain the learner’s own revision. Use the NS+ prompt and learner response in their own colour before recording R. E means evidence actually banked in the school's evidence record, not a promise to upload.
Private help and assessment boundary

Identify the school support route. Listen without investigating in class; never promise secrecy. Use the local safeguarding procedure, separate from lesson evidence.
